title: admin-plugin-marketplace: curated remediation recipes and staged dry-run
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Problem: On-call engineers frequently run ad-hoc admin scripts during incidents and inconsistently apply safety checks (RBAC, dry-run, tenancy). This causes variability in remediation quality and occasional user downtime.

Goal: Build an "admin plugin marketplace" — a curated registry of small, versioned remediation "recipes" (tasklets) that can be discovered from the Console/CLI, executed in staged modes (preview/dry-run -> canary -> full), and automatically gated by policies (RBAC, capacity, cooldown). Recipes are authored as opinionated task definitions (typed inputs, expected outputs, telemetry hooks) and packaged as immutable artifacts with provenance.

Scope: MVP focuses on: (1) recipe registry service + metadata API, (2) CLI/Console discovery UI, (3) staged execution modes with simulated dry-run, (4) mandatory safety checks (policy evaluation, explicit reviewer requirement for high-impact recipes), (5) telemetry & SLO signals for recipe success/failure/rollbacks.

Non-goals: Not shipping an authoring DSL in MVP (authors will use an internal template); not migrating existing ad-hoc scripts into marketplace for launch.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Registry API exists (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) with ACL enforced and audit log entries for create/update/execute.
- CLI command `redwood admin catalog list|describe|run --mode={preview|canary|apply}` implemented and documented.
- Dry-run mode executes recipe against a sanitized simulator environment and emits a diff-based preview.
- Canary mode applies recipe to a small slice (configurable target set) and collects metrics for 15m before auto-promote/rollback.
- All recipe executions produce traceable telemetry (trace id, run id) and surface in Console runbook timeline.
- PR with unit + integration tests merged; e2e smoke test that runs preview -> canary -> apply flows in staging.

Design notes / Trade-offs: 
- Registry stores recipe metadata (id, version, checksum, manifest) and an S3-backed artifact for executable payload. We accept up to 50ms extra latency on registry reads because read cache will be fronted by CDN.
- For MVP we require recipes to declare an impact level tag (low/medium/high) and disallow auto-apply for high; this avoids complex static analysis.
- Dry-run implemented via a simulation harness (lightweight VCR-style mocks + a safety fake backend) to avoid touching production systems. This increases test coverage at cost of maintaining mocks.
- We will not support arbitrary code execution in the registry (only curated, built artifacts signed by CI). This reduces risk but requires a review pipeline for new recipes.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) API + DB schema for registry (postgres table: recipe, version, metadata, owner, impact_level, checksum).
2) Artifact storage in customer-siloed S3 bucket with KMS encryption and signed URLs for executor.
3) Executor shim service that pulls artifact, verifies checksum & signature, runs in sandboxed worker with policy agent (OPA) eval before each step.
4) CLI/Console integration: list/describe/run flows + staged mode flags.
5) Simulation harness for preview with a corpus of canned responses and diff renderer.
6) Telemetry: Run events (start/end/status), traces, metric buckets (success_rate, latency, rollback_rate).
7) RBAC & audit integration (SSO groups -> allowed impact levels).

Security & compliance: Artifacts must be CI-signed; execution workers run in isolated container runtime with strict egress rules; KMS keys used for artifact encryption; all actions produce audit logs forwarded to SIEM. Security review scheduled with @Nadia (Sec) before enabling apply mode for high-impact recipes.

Rollout plan: Beta to internal SRE and support teams for 2 weeks (staging environment), then opt-in in one region for customer-facing incidents. Monitor rollback_rate and user-reported regressions for 7 days before wider rollout.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Mock divergence in dry-run causing false confidence. Mitigation: maintain small set of canonical simulation cases and require recipe authors to add simulation scenarios.
- Risk: Accidental privilege escalation. Mitigation: sign-off gate + reviewer + policy engine enforced at execution time.
